clue.text: Redirected to study creating in small-scale business

indicators.note: something redirected is sent off along a different route, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: three words used letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Someone has been sent off to study how to set up a small business of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder runs across three words, which hides how much of the clue is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage industry is a business carried on at home on a modest scale, originally weaving or similar craft work.

clue.text: Observe and act, bringing in power for car part

indicators.note: bringing something in takes it inside the word that does the bringing

parts.note: to observe is to see
P is the physics symbol for power
to act is to do

explanation.surface: An instruction to watch and then do something, as if learning to fit a component to a car.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDO is short for speedometer, the dial on a dashboard showing how fast the car is going.
explanation.definitionFit: A speedometer, shortened in everyday speech, is the dashboard instrument fitted to every vehicle to show its speed.

clue.text: Phi, mostly, with pi and psi initially turning up in lab items?

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the string is read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
mostly means not quite all of it, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: Phi is the pseudonym of this puzzle's setter
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points at only the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of the Greek letter's name

explanation.surface: A self-referential joke: Greek letters phi, pi and psi turning up in a science lab, as on equipment labels.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter uses his own name: Phi stands for SETTER, cut to SETTE. With PI and P added, the whole string is reversed to give PIPETTES.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipettes are slender graduated tubes used in laboratories for measuring and transferring small volumes of liquid.

clue.text: Animal transport tethered if shops around

indicators.note: around suggests letters scattered about rather than kept in line, so they are reordered

parts.note: three words used letter for letter as raw material

explanation.surface: Pack animals hitched up outside some shops, as in a market town.
explanation.definitionFit: The camel is nicknamed the ship of the desert, being the traditional beast for carrying people and goods across sand.

clue.text: Reach area, ready to accept cheers

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: something that accepts takes another thing inside it

parts.note: both ready and tin are slang for cash
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Getting to a place that is prepared to welcome visitors with a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' reads as an adjective but is the British slang noun for money, as in 'the ready', and so is tin; ta and cheers both mean thanks in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal or position is to reach it, especially after effort, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: River running through farm fodder — amount lost?

indicators.note: a stream running through something passes inside it

parts.note: silage is fermented grass stored as winter feed for livestock
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A river flooding through stored animal feed, with the farmer wondering how much has been ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: spoilage is the amount of goods wasted by going bad.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoilage means the quantity of food or material wasted through decay or damage, so it measures what has gone.

clue.text: Obscure bag filled with bananas is wishful thinking

indicators.note: something filled with an item holds it inside, between its outer parts

parts.note: to obscure something is to cloud it, as a verb
to bag is to land or catch, as a verb
both are slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A shopping bag full of bananas, compared with an unrealistic dream.
explanation.walkthrough: Obscure and bag look like adjective and noun but are both verbs; the two words they give sit either side of the slang word for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land, from Aristophanes' The Birds, is an imaginary realm of impractical fantasy where hopeful dreamers live.

clue.text: Bathroom item seen in meal on TV programme?

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed on means written after the word that follows

parts.note: a soap is a TV serial drama
a dish is a meal or course

explanation.surface: Spotting a kitchen item in the food on a television cookery show.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap dish is the small tray beside a sink or bath that holds the bar of soap.

clue.text: Upset with excuse after dropping a drink

indicators.note: after places what follows behind what came before it

parts.note: to upset is to tip over

indicators.note: dropping something lets it fall away and be left out

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered
the letter taken out

explanation.surface: Someone upset and making excuses for spilling a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset reads as an emotion but means knock over; the excuse loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is a person's usual alcoholic beverage, and as a verb it means to drink habitually.

clue.text: Worried about female deity

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: worried means ate, as in what's eating you
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Someone anxious about a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: Worried looks like an adjective but is a past-tense verb: to eat at someone is to worry them.
explanation.definitionFit: Athene, also spelt Athena, is the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, patron of Athens.

clue.text: Group with a recording turning over millions — going this?

definitions.note: the answer completes 'going ___', the clue's phrase for a record selling a million

indicators.note: turning something over flips it end to end, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a unit is a group
taken as written
an LP is a long-playing record
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A band with a record turning over millions in sales, asking what status it has reached.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over millions' sounds like sales, but turning over acts only on the group, a and recording; millions is then added on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A record goes platinum when its sales pass a top threshold, earning a platinum disc award.

clue.text: Say second new theme's beginning in Beethoven overture

parts.note: e.g. means for example, as say does
a mo is a moment or second
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A music analysis note about a fresh second theme starting in a Beethoven overture.
explanation.definitionFit: Egmont is Beethoven's overture and incidental music for Goethe's play about the Flemish count Egmont.

clue.text: Enthusiast caught engaging in some European risqué entertainment

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

indicators.note: to engage in is to be caught up inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A keen follower caught up in some saucy show while travelling in Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan dance is a cabaret routine in which a dancer, apparently nude, is concealed by large feathered fans.

clue.text: Member's upward path, dislodging leader

indicators.note: dislodging the leader knocks off the front letter

parts.note: a climb is a path going upward

explanation.surface: A club member's route to promotion, after ousting the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Member's reads as a possessive but is 'member is'; member is the body-part sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A limb is an arm or leg, and member is an old word for any such part of the body.

clue.text: Defender leading others in support

indicators.note: in a down clue, leading places one part first, on top of the next

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A footballer heading a team-mates' show of support.
explanation.definitionFit: A backrest is the part of a seat that supports your back when leaning against it.

clue.text: School with a dull sound

parts.note: SCH is the abbreviation for school
W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A school whose bell, or reputation, has a flat ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A schwa is the neutral, unstressed vowel heard in 'about' or 'sofa', the most indistinct sound in English.

clue.text: Inactivity? A pop star will have change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart here means the central letter is swapped for another

parts.note: taken as written
Beyoncé is the American singer

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a famous singer has gone quiet after changing her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the star's name, O, is replaced by the A of the clue's change.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeyance is a state of temporary suspension, when a matter is put on hold and nothing happens.

clue.text: Do some artistic work — a quantity of sketching?

indicators.note: a quantity of something is only part of it, so a run of letters is taken

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: Asking whether drawing counts as artistic work.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to make a picture by cutting lines into a metal plate with acid, an artist's printmaking technique.

clue.text: Erudite Cockney's attention monopolised by old coin? On the contrary

indicators.note: a thing monopolised by another is held inside it
this reverses the stated roles, so the holder becomes the held
Cockneys famously drop the H sound at the start of words

parts.note: to pay heed is to pay attention
the ducat was a gold coin of old Europe

explanation.surface: A learned East Ender absorbed in an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary flips the container: the coin goes inside the Cockney word, not the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated and erudite both describe someone who has learned a great deal through schooling and study.

clue.text: Tense four terms in Sherborne suppressing Henry's laugh

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: suppressing something holds it down within

parts.note: a term is an end, and the word's last letter is taken four times
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A tense time at Sherborne, a Dorset public school, where a boy called Henry stifles a giggle.
explanation.walkthrough: Terms reads as school terms, but means terminal letters: four of the town's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is the written imitation of a stifled giggle or snigger, used as a noun or interjection.

clue.text: The writer returned work containing zero engagement

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: the writer refers to the setter, me

indicators.note: containing means holding something inside

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: An author coming back to a job with no commitments.
explanation.definitionFit: Employ as a noun means the state of being hired, as in 'in his employ', which is an engagement.

clue.text: Study essentially involving university

indicators.note: something involving another wraps it up inside

parts.note: per se means in itself, essentially
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A student reading the essentials while at university.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine something carefully, which is a way to study it.

clue.text: They seize American person touring Biblical city

indicators.note: touring means going round, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for American
pers is the abbreviation for person
Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's birthplace in Genesis

explanation.surface: An American tourist visiting a city from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Usurpers are people who take a throne or power by force, so seizing what is not theirs.

clue.text: Texted expression of affection after song with little substance

indicators.note: after places this part behind the one named next

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
text shorthand for I love you

explanation.surface: A love-text tacked onto a slight, flimsy pop song.
explanation.definitionFit: Airily means lightly or flippantly, without weight or seriousness, as though made of air.

clue.text: Conservative trick to suppress old isolated figure

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: to suppress something is to hold it down inside

parts.note: a ruse is a trick
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A political party using a dodge to sideline an elderly, lonely member.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe, Defoe's castaway, lived alone on a desert island for years, the archetypal isolated man.

clue.text: Dissenter to renounce belief about our group

indicators.note: about means around, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to recant is to take back a held belief
us is the speakers' own group

explanation.surface: A rebel being made to abandon faith in their own circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony: a recusant refuses to conform, the opposite of one who recants.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a recusant was someone, usually Catholic, refusing to attend Church of England services, hence any dissenter.
